contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #235: Limiting random SAT thresholds, sharp variance and computability.

Audit the universal pathwise continuation-law records ctr:record in ct:old-records and ct:new-record of the staged September 27, 2026 computability manuscript; distinguish this bridge from the main SAT threshold and endpoint claims.

definitions.record: For each specified continuous test, squared L2 error over ancestor site uniforms is at most delta squared for almost every fixed complete global path, including the root.
definitions.representation: Finite-depth product-tree representation with independent uniform generators paired with the site root (globals) and each individual site.
definitions.joint_record: For J tests the sum of their squared L2 errors is at most 2 J gamma, a stronger simultaneous conclusion than the individual records.

claims.natural_statement: In every represented hierarchy obtained by the manuscript construction, all old ctr:record bounds are preserved with unchanged tolerance, and the new block satisfies ctr:record for every specified finite continuous test family and delta greater than zero, for almost every complete global path. The record argument does not assert correctness of the separate endpoint functional passage.

For arbitrary fixed finite depth and continuous type tests, old pathwise squared-L2 records survive fresh-site-preserving absolutely continuous posterior changes, weak limits of the decorated natural arrays, countable partition-selected reindexing preserving old prefixes, and the represented hierarchy, without increasing delta.

For every finite nonempty family of J continuous [0,1]-valued tests, a scalar overlap support band of width gamma for pairs branching below the new boundary gives one ancestor-measurable probability type with each squared-L2 error at most 2 J gamma; gamma at most delta squared divided by 2 J yields exactly the advertised record.

Synchronization-free joint-record theorem: in the represented hierarchy, if the scalar averaged test Gram overlap of two conditionally independent continuation branches lies in one fixed closed interval of width gamma almost surely, then the conditional continuation-law type has the sum of all J squared-L2 test errors at most 2 J gamma for almost every complete global path. No componentwise ordering of vector overlaps or finite overlap support is required.

For any probability law on a separable real Hilbert space, an almost-sure absolute inner-product bound delta squared for two independent copies implies squared norm at most delta squared almost surely. A closed overlap interval of width epsilon implies squared support diameter at most 2 epsilon and the same squared-radius bound around any point of the closed convex hull, hence the barycenter. This includes arbitrary infinite-dimensional laws, not only finite models.

Uniform finite-column squared-distance-to-a-closed-interval estimates at most 1/I pass to weak limits of compact decorated arrays; along dyadic I they force the limiting site empirical products into that interval simultaneously for every countable deterministic path tuple, hence also for every partition-selected tuple.

The scalar marked-Ghirlanda-Guerra cut predictions imply that, conditional on the full nested partition, every finite decoration tuple has a law depending only on its internal cut pattern; partition-measurable ranked reindexing consequently preserves the required hierarchical exchangeabilities and separates decorations from the partition.

For independent proper uniformly signed 3-clauses sampled with replacement, there is alpha_3 in (0,infinity) with strict-side satisfiability limits, and one deterministic oracle-free Turing machine returns a rational within 2^(-r) of alpha_3 and halts for every unary precision input 1^r.
For every a greater than zero and finite beta greater than zero, the pressure equals the infimum of G_1 over finite-depth strict rational site-only trials; closure.tex cc:complete.

Recorded conditional continuation laws permit replacement of nonroot globals by site sampling with the explicit cutoff, exponent-width, kernel-error, and small-first-exponent bound of closure.tex cc:kernel-collapse.

Under the full fixed-depth active-trial hypotheses ct:input-bound, ctr:band, and ctr:record, ct:transition produces for every fixed output horizon k a trial of value G_k/k at most U, inserts at most two levels, preserves old records, creates a new record, and either reaches the root or reduces the first exponent by a factor at most 1-eta.

For every fixed integer k at least 3, independent proper uniformly signed k-clauses sampled with replacement have a limiting threshold alpha_k in (0,infinity), with satisfiability limits 1 strictly below and 0 strictly above.
The capped last-satisfiable index V_n=min(H_n-1,L_k n) has variance O_k(n^(1+2/k)); the resulting polynomial tail estimate feeds concentration-to-convergence.

Interior finite-size means and a polynomial sublinear concentration bound imply convergence to a strict-side proper-clause threshold through auxiliary interpolation, proper-clause transfer, and balanced center comparisons.

For proper independent uniformly signed k-clauses with fixed k at least 3, Var(H_n) is at most C_k n log(en) for k=3 and C_k n for k at least 4, and at least c_k n eventually. Every fixed linear cap has the corresponding upper bound; caps above U_k have the eventual lower bound.
For every assignment set S on u at least k variables and d at least 1, with beta=k/(k-1), the shorter-clause killing probability obeys tau_k(S) q_d(S)^beta at most C_k d^beta.

The environment-conditional occupation bound sums P(S_m nonempty,q_d(S_m) at least a) to at most min(L,C_k d^beta a^(-beta)); integrating it and averaging weighted root-collision moments bounds squared deletion delays.
For proper independent uniformly signed 3-clauses with replacement, an absolute C gives Var(H_n) at most C n for every n at least 3, and an absolute positive c gives Var(H_n) at least c n eventually.
For every nonempty assignment set on u variables and d at least 1, beta=3/2 and P_d=sum_{j<d}q_j, q_d(S)^beta is at most d^(beta-1) times (3 E_C[P_d(S[C])-P_d(S)]+d u^(-3)); source lem:potential.

The potential-drift bound together with independent root-flip tests gives a uniform O(1) squared clause-omission delay after averaging incidence and collision counts, yielding the linear capped variance bound and then the uncapped bound.

For any probability law on a separable real Hilbert space, an almost-sure absolute inner-product bound delta squared for two independent copies implies squared norm at most delta squared almost surely. A closed overlap interval of width epsilon implies squared support diameter at most 2 epsilon and the same squared-radius bound around any point of the closed convex hull, hence the barycenter. This includes arbitrary infinite-dimensional laws, not only finite models.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace RecordTransfer

variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
  [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H]

theorem pair_interval_on_support
    (μ : Measure H) (a b : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a b) :
    ∀ v ∈ μ.support, ∀ w ∈ μ.support, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a b := by
  have hsections : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ w ∈ μ.support, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a b := by
    filter_upwards [h] with v hv
    exact μ.support_subset_of_isClosed
      (isClosed_Icc.preimage (continuous_const.inner continuous_id)) hv
  intro v hv w hw
  have hw_ae : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ⟪x, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a b :=
    hsections.mono fun x hx => hx w hw
  exact μ.support_subset_of_isClosed
    (isClosed_Icc.preimage (continuous_id.inner continuous_const)) hw_ae hv

theorem old_record_on_support
    (μ : Measure H) (δ : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, |⟪v, w⟫_ℝ| ≤ δ ^ 2) :
    ∀ v ∈ μ.support, ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ δ ^ 2 := by
  have hp : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc (-(δ ^ 2)) (δ ^ 2) := by
    filter_upwards [h] with v hv
    filter_upwards [hv] with w hw
    exact abs_le.mp hw
  intro v hv
  have hdiag := (pair_interval_on_support μ _ _ hp v hv v hv).2
  simpa only [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq] using hdiag

theorem band_diameter_on_support
    (μ : Measure H) (a ε : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a (a + ε)) :
    ∀ v ∈ μ.support, ∀ w ∈ μ.support, ‖v - w‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ε := by
  have hp := pair_interval_on_support μ a (a + ε) h
  intro v hv w hw
  have hvv := (hp v hv v hv).2
  have hww := (hp w hw w hw).2
  have hvw := (hp v hv w hw).1
  rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq] at hvv hww
  rw [norm_sub_sq_real]
  linarith

theorem band_center_on_support
    (μ : Measure H) (a ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (h : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a (a + ε))
    (m : H) (hm : m ∈ closedConvexHull ℝ μ.support) :
    ∀ v ∈ μ.support, ‖v - m‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ε := by
  intro v hv
  have hrad : 0 ≤ 2 * ε := mul_nonneg (by norm_num) hε
  have hsqrt := Real.sq_sqrt hrad
  have hsqrtn := Real.sqrt_nonneg (2 * ε)
  have hball : μ.support ⊆ Metric.closedBall v (Real.sqrt (2 * ε)) := by
    intro w hw
    have hdist := band_diameter_on_support μ a ε h v hv w hw
    have hn := norm_nonneg (v - w)
    have hle : ‖v - w‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (2 * ε) := by nlinarith
    simpa only [Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev] using hle
  have hm_ball : m ∈ Metric.closedBall v (Real.sqrt (2 * ε)) :=
    closedConvexHull_min hball (convex_closedBall v _) isClosed_closedBall hm
  have hnorm : ‖v - m‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (2 * ε) := by
    simpa only [Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev] using hm_ball
  have hn := norm_nonneg (v - m)
  nlinarith

theorem old_record_ae
    [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure H) (δ : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, |⟪v, w⟫_ℝ| ≤ δ ^ 2) :
    ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ δ ^ 2 :=
  μ.support_mem_ae.mono fun v hv => old_record_on_support μ δ h v hv

theorem band_center_ae
    [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure H) (a ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (h : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a (a + ε))
    (m : H) (hm : m ∈ closedConvexHull ℝ μ.support) :
    ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ‖v - m‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ε :=
  μ.support_mem_ae.mono fun v hv => band_center_on_support μ a ε hε h m hm v hv

theorem advertised_tolerance
    (errorSq J γ δ : ℝ) (hJ : 0 < J)
    (herror : errorSq ≤ 2 * J * γ)
    (hγ : γ ≤ δ ^ 2 / (2 * J)) :
    errorSq ≤ δ ^ 2 := by
  have hden : 0 < 2 * J := mul_pos (by norm_num) hJ
  have hbound := (le_div_iff₀ hden).mp hγ
  nlinarith

end RecordTransfer

#print axioms RecordTransfer.pair_interval_on_support
#print axioms RecordTransfer.old_record_ae
#print axioms RecordTransfer.band_center_ae
#print axioms RecordTransfer.advertised_tolerance

  exact hs.mono fun v hv => old_record_on_support μ δ h v hv

theorem band_center_ae
    [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure H) (a ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (h : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ∀ᵐ w ∂μ, ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ ∈ Icc a (a + ε))
    (m : H) (hm : m ∈ closedConvexHull ℝ μ.support) :
    ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, ‖v - m‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * ε := by
  have hs : ∀ᵐ v ∂μ, v ∈ μ.support := μ.support_mem_ae
  exact hs.mono fun v hv => band_center_on_support μ a ε hε h m hm v hv

theorem advertised_tolerance
    (errorSq J γ δ : ℝ) (hJ : 0 < J)
    (herror : errorSq ≤ 2 * J * γ)
    (hγ : γ ≤ δ ^ 2 / (2 * J)) :
    errorSq ≤ δ ^ 2 := by
  have hden : 0 < 2 * J := mul_pos (by norm_num) hJ
  have hbound := (le_div_iff₀ hden).mp hγ
  nlinarith

end RecordTransfer
